about: tareplay's fixtures (tools/replay/tareplay.py). Each is a scripted skirmish recorded live and then checked on puppets. `load` is a scenario under scenarios/; `steps` run at a GameTime of the live game, which starts held at GameTime 1 with its scenario applied (tareplay.py, THE LAUNCH'S HOLD), each given while the game is held at its GameTime: `apply` a scenario, `type` a chat line, `keys` native input tokens, `order` one unit by roster type and rank; `last_min` requires the final comparison checkpoint to reach that GameTime; `end` is the GameTime scenarios/replay-end.json ends the level at. `los`: "file" keeps the scenario's own line of sight, else the SkirmishLineOfSight value. `dll`: "stock" plays the stock-limits build. `content`: a command run before every launch of the fixture ({gamedir} the instance's game folder) and the files it writes there, which every other fixture's launch removes first. `unit_limit`: the game's unit limit, 500 unless given. `takeover`: the fixture is also taken over (tareplay.py's K and F): at T2, or at `at` when given (tenseat's: 901, the tick after its typed LOS command, where a takeover's contact bits must come from the recording), as `player` (a record, or "controlled", the recording's controlled player), with the `switches` set and the chat line `type` typed after the takeover, `order` (a type and rank of the player's units) moved 300 wu, K's dump `dump` ticks after T (1800 unless given), and the `checks` it must pass (TAKEOVER_CHECKS); a takeover with `victory` ends by its own chat line (`+iwin`: the console's Kill disarms the objective, so `+kill` never ends a level), any other by replay-end.json. `rewind`: adds the U live-rewind lane; `rewind_steps`: extra scripted steps applied to its live run; `rewind_paused` names the scenario applied while paused just before its saved-present dump. `broad` holds what only the broad tier runs (tareplay.py broad): `trips`, round trips beyond the three; `cost`, a game recorded live and reported for the recorder's cost and the file's size, with no check. `run` steps execute an assertion command ({instance} and {gamedir} substitutions), handed the game held at their GameTime and handing it back held where they advanced it, and fail the live lane on a nonzero exit; a later step's GameTime must lie past where its script leaves the game. `sources` binds input/presentation code to replay fixtures in addition to the SIM_FEATURE gates. `preflight` runs a native assertion before the live recording starts. `viewer` and `viewer_more` run native input assertions in separate paused selection views, each checked against the same frozen simulation. `cob`: "exact" compares L's counts against P's with `tarec compare-counts --cob-exact`, every COB child the VM's START or CALL makes, by script name, exactly, and no other comparison (tareplay.py, counts_options). `forest-reproduce` and `stock-forest-reproduce` install tools/reproduce_fixture.py's archive (the stock twin on feat-forest.json's quiet forest: a seek in the stock-limits build does not put back the burning trees' explosions in stock's pool, which s3a-forest-fire.json's fire keeps in flight), so the trees and shrubs the feature cursor passes reproduce: Two Continents has trees at rest in its last rows, which the cursor, one cell a tick from the map's last, reaches from about GameTime 360, and each one's spawn makes reproduction's source test (tagpu_recorder.c, feat_source) in both builds. `decline`: every launch has tagpu_rec.decline in its game folder, so the writer's stream codec declines blocks 2, 7, 12, ... through its own fallback, and the recording must count declined blocks (tareplay.py, codec_check); every other check reads across them.
